proposal.expected_benefit: This change will prevent replay attacks by ensuring that intentIds are uniquely consumed and cannot be reused, even with different PoI hashes.
proposal.problem: The system currently rejects duplicate PoI hashes but does not enforce on-chain rejection of reused intentIds with different PoI hashes, creating a potential replay attack vector.
proposal.proposed_change: Implement a policy that enforces on-chain rejection of any intentId that has been previously used, regardless of the PoI hash, to prevent intentId reuse attacks.

risks.description: Introducing a new policy may inadvertently block legitimate intentId reuse scenarios that are valid under the current system.
risks.mitigation: Implement a rollback plan and conduct a controlled test phase before full deployment.

proposal.rollback_plan: If the policy causes unintended behavior or conflicts with existing contracts, revert to the previous intent validation logic and re-evaluate the policy with additional constraints or exceptions.
security_invariants: All intentIds must be unique and cannot be reused across any transaction.
The system must maintain immutability of contract behavior and not bypass any existing audit or compliance controls.
proposal.title: IntentId Reuse Detection Policy Enhancement

verification_tests.description: Simulate a replay attack by reusing an intentId with a different PoI hash and verify that the system correctly rejects it.
verification_tests.expected_result: The system must reject the intentId reuse attempt with a clear error message.

verification_tests.description: Verify that the system allows the same intentId to be used only once, even if the PoI hash changes.
verification_tests.expected_result: The system must enforce intentId uniqueness across all transactions.
